title: Dynamics 365 Business Central UI performance: what about the browser and the local machine?
summary: Business Central UI performance depends on network latency, browser capabilities, and local machine hardware, not just backend optimization. The post explains how to measure and monitor these client-side factors during go-live and production.
key_points: Network latency to Azure datacenters should be 250-300ms or less; higher latency significantly impacts perceived slowness
Modern browsers (Edge, Chrome, Safari) with adequate storage and proper configuration are essential; multiple tabs consume resources and add ~10 seconds per tab
Local machine hardware (CPU, RAM, GPU, storage) directly affects browser rendering and JavaScript execution; 16GB+ RAM and Apple Silicon devices perform best
Page View telemetry provides network metrics; monitoring tools like Speedometer 3.1 benchmark and custom Node.js scripts help measure actual performance
Client-side factors are often overlooked in infrastructure assessments but can have considerable impact on end-user experience despite backend optimizations

quotes.text: Business Central is designed for networks that have a latency of 250 - 300 milliseconds (ms) or less.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the key performance threshold for network latency that organizations must meet
